title: ChatCompletions legacy client semantics preserver
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Provide a compatibility translation layer that preserves behavioral semantics expected by legacy OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) clients while routing to Redwood’s native streaming + function-calling runtime. Scope includes request field mapping, streaming chunk framing, tool/function_call lifecycle, structured output enforcement, idempotency/seq IDs, and telemetry parity. This ticket covers design, infra adapters, and a non-breaking rollout plan for self-serve hosted API users.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OpenAI ChatCompletions requests are accepted on /v1/chat/completions and translated to Redwood internal request model with no observable semantic regressions for existing legacy clients.
Streaming responses over SSE/HTTP chunked transfer present equivalent event/frame order and token deltas as legacy clients expect (function_call start/content/end events preserved).

Function/tool calling semantics (name, arguments, call lifecycle) are faithfully reproduced and routed to Redwood tool hooks; downstream tool errors surfaced in the same shape as OpenAI clients expect.
Structured output helpers (content-type hints, JSON schema enforcement) are applied without dropping legacy freeform outputs unless requested by the downstream model config.
Automated conformance suite passes for 95% of sampled legacy client integration tests; remaining diffs documented and classified as acceptable or blockers.
Telemetry: token-level latency, function-call durations, and stream chunk counts reported on the Console per-route dashboard for migrated requests.
No customer-facing downtime during canary rollout and automatic fallback to pre-compat path if mapping errors exceed threshold.
technical_design: We will implement a thin compatibility adapter in the API gateway layer that performs deterministic mappings from OpenAI Chat Completions payloads to Redwood’s native request model. Key pieces: 1) Request normalization: map 'messages' -> conversation segments, detect 'temperature/top_p' semantics and convert to internal sampling params; preserve role/name metadata. 2) Streaming frame adapter: translate internal streaming frames into legacy SSE/delta messages with explicit function_call framing (start/content/end) and incremental JSON assembly for structured outputs. 3) Function call lifecycle: provide an in-proxy function_call mediator that records call intent, serializes arguments per legacy expectations, awaits tool execution, and injects tool result events into the stream with original metadata. 4) Schema/structured-output enforcement: optional post-token validation pass using lightweight JSON schema checks; on schema violation, attach a 'content_warning' field rather than mutating original output. 5) Idempotency and dedup: respect client-supplied 'idempotency_key' header and maintain 24h cache for retried requests. 6) Error semantics: map internal errors to OpenAI-style error objects, including type/code/message and partial_response handling. 7) Telemetry: emit compatibility-layer spans and metrics (mapping_latency_ms, stream_chunks_emitted, function_call_duration_ms) to tracing and Console. 8) Performance: adapter is implemented in Rust/pfast path and benchmarks should show <1ms median added latency for non-streaming requests and <5% throughput regression under heavy streaming workloads.
implementation_notes: Add gateway adapter module under api-gateway/compat/openai_chat_v1
Create feature flag 'oa_cc_compat_v1' to gate rollout by customer and route
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/6789 - telemetry dashboard widgets for compatibility metrics
Add lightweight JSON schema validator dependency (must be optional at runtime)
Update rate-limiter mappings to account for token accounting differences between legacy and Redwood tokenizers
test_plan: Unit: mapping functions for roles/messages/params with fuzz inputs
Integration: end-to-end tests against a reference legacy client emulator that validates SSE frames and tool_call events
Conformance: run existing OA CC compatibility test suite (500+ scenarios) and record diffs
Perf: synthetic load test for streaming with 500 concurrent streams for 30m comparing pre/post adapter P95 latency and throughput
Chaos: introduce partial tool timeouts and validate fallback semantics and error mapping
Canary: 1% of traffic both internal and a small set of opt-in customers for 48h before ramping
risks_mitigation: Risk: subtle semantics drift for edge-case role/name combinations. Mitigation: include sample corpus from customer telemetry to run compatibility checks and maintain a 'semantic diff' dashboard.
Risk: streaming reordering under backpressure. Mitigation: enforce per-request sequence numbers and buffer window with configurable max-latency for preservation.
Risk: increased gateway CPU due to JSON schema checks. Mitigation: schema checks optional and done in background for streaming; warm path avoids heavy validation.
Risk: exposing internal data in compatibility wrapper. Mitigation: adapter sanitizes metadata and enforces PII redact rules from Privacy team guidance.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal testing - feature flag enabled for staging and internal apps only
Phase 1 (Canary): enable 'oa_cc_compat_v1' for 1% hosted API traffic and 3 opt-in customers for 48 hours; monitor errors and latency
Phase 2 (Ramp): 10% -> 50% over 1 week if metrics stable, notify Customer Success for opt-in outreach
Phase 3 (GA): enable for all hosted traffic, provide docs for Dedicated/Private customers to opt-in and run local adapter if needed
Rollback: automatic disable if error_rate > 0.5% or P95 latency regression > 30% over baseline
